text:
lee_support: forwarding a customer escalation — they saw a ~$1.2k invoice jump overnight and are certain usage didn't change much. They attached a curl and their SDK snippet. invoice: INV-2026-11-02-9923

lee_support: curl they used (redacted keys):
```bash
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"open-compat-1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize logs"}],"stream":true}'
```

anna_support: ouch. which SDK and version? streaming true might affect local estimator.

lee_support: customer says SDK v0.9.2 (node). they called streaming and often stop the stream early in their UI. they also use a server-side middleware that injects a small tool output (JSON metadata) after generation.

metering_bot: Automated alert: spike detected for account acct-3345, +$1,213 vs baseline; sample request_id: r-8b2c7a

devon_engineer: looking at our metering logs for r-8b2c7a — server shows additional 3 system/tool segments inserted post-generation (kv-prefill + tool-result metadata). Each insertion counts ~45-120 tokens depending on payload. SDK estimator often omits server-injected tool metadata.

devon_engineer: TL;DR probable causes: (1) server-inserted tool/system messages (hidden to client estimator) (2) streaming early-stop vs final completion counting differences (3) function/tool-call results persisted into session KV and re-sent on subsequent requests.

anna_support: can we repro quickly with their exact flow? lee, ask customer to run a non-streaming curl (stream:false) and also one streaming curl but with header X-Redwood-Debug: meter,true and send us the X-Redwood-Request-Id.

lee_support: sent repro steps. customer returned these two request_ids: r-8b2c7a (streaming) and r-8b2c7b (non-streaming). They included SDK-estimator outputs: estimator claimed ~280 tokens per request, invoice shows ~640 tokens.

devon_engineer: I pulled both request traces. For r-8b2c7a (streaming) our runtime still accounted for the final stop tokenization bucket — even though client closed the stream mid-completion, the server had already generated post-EOF tool metadata which gets serialized and metered. For r-8b2c7b (non-streaming) there's explicit tool/result embedding of ~330 tokens returned as metadata. SDK estimator v0.9.2 ignores metadata fields named x-tool-result or sidecar by default.

sophie_billing: billing side: invoice meter matches server-trace token tally. We can't adjust billed usage without a clear undercount bug in metering. If the SDK undercounts customer-visible tokens we can provide a credit but need repeatable repro and timeline.

devon_engineer: repro steps for customer (minimal):
1) run curl non-streaming with explicit header to surface all metadata: 
   -H "X-Redwood-Meter-Expose: full"
2) save both response body and response headers (look for x-redwood-metering-summary and x-redwood-request-id)
3) run node SDK v0.9.2 with estimator enabled and dump estimator.token_count and raw response tokens.
4) share both outputs + the two request ids.

devon_engineer: quick internal note: we should update SDK docs to warn about server-injected tool/system messages and provide a compatibility flag. Also consider adding an optional x-metering-sample payload to allow client estimate to include server-side post-process tokens.

anna_support: adding a short checklist for Lee to include in the customer reply so billing can act fast:
- provide request ids for all disputed invoices
- include SDK version and whether streaming was used
- attach both curl (non-stream) and SDK run outputs
- include any middleware that adds tool outputs or persists session KV

lee_support: will send that now. customer asked whether short-term mitigation exists — can we suggest disabling streaming or set server-side middleware to not attach tool metadata?

devon_engineer: mitigation: temporarily disable streaming or move tool results to a separate endpoint (not returned inline) so they don't inflate per-request meter. Also they can pin session-less requests so KV-prefill isn't sent.

sophie_billing: once customer provides repro we can run an audit and if we confirm SDK under-reporting vs server meter we can issue a one-time adjustment. please cc billing with request ids.

lee_support: thanks — I'll follow up with the customer and collect the two traces. marking this thread as needs-repro. :white_check_mark:
